title: Two-sided nondegenerate finite-dimensional field pairings are perfect
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $M,N$ be $K$-vector spaces, with $M$ finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Let $p:M\times N\to K$ be bilinear, meaning linear in each variable. Suppose that $p(x,y)=0$ for every $y\in N$ implies $x=0$, and that $p(x,y)=0$ for every $x\in M$ implies $y=0$. Then both induced linear maps
$$M\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_K(N,K),\quad x\longmapsto p(x,-),\qquad N\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,K),\quad y\longmapsto p(-,y)$$
are isomorphisms.

source.place: Chapter I §13, pp.57–58, linear algebra used after rationalizing the finite Weil pairing. Exact general statement in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/PerfectPairing/Basic.lean:116.
